Words2Numbers.__init__:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Initializes the number-word lookup tables and ordinal suffix rules used to parse English number words into numeric values." __init__]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Create an empty dictionary and assign it to self.numwords. RESULT self.numwords]
            [COMMAND Define self.units as the list of English cardinal number words from 'zero' through 'nineteen': zero, one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen. RESULT self.units]
            [COMMAND Define self.tens as the list containing empty strings at indices 0 and 1, followed by 'twenty', 'thirty', 'forty', 'fifty', 'sixty', 'seventy', 'eighty', and 'ninety' at indices 2 through 9. RESULT self.tens]
            [COMMAND Define self.scales as the list containing 'hundred', 'thousand', 'million', 'billion', and 'trillion'. RESULT self.scales]
            [COMMAND Insert the sentinel mapping for the word 'and' as the tuple (1, 0) into self.numwords. RESULT self.numwords]
            [COMMAND For each unit word at index idx in self.units, map the word to the tuple (1, idx) in self.numwords. RESULT self.numwords]
            [COMMAND For each tens word at index idx in self.tens, map the word to the tuple (1, idx * 10) in self.numwords. RESULT self.numwords]
            [COMMAND For each scale word at index idx in self.scales, map the word to the tuple (10 ** (idx * 3 or 2), 0) in self.numwords, so idx 0 produces 100 and later indices produce powers of 1000. RESULT self.numwords]
            [COMMAND Define self.ordinal_words as the dictionary containing irregular ordinal mappings 'first' to 1, 'second' to 2, 'third' to 3, 'fifth' to 5, 'eighth' to 8, 'ninth' to 9, and 'twelfth' to 12. RESULT self.ordinal_words]
            [COMMAND Define self.ordinal_endings as the ordered list of suffix replacement pairs ('ieth' replaced by 'y') and ('th' replaced by an empty string), preserving the given order so 'ieth' is matched before 'th'. RESULT self.ordinal_endings]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
Words2Numbers.text2int:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Converts a string containing spelled-out number words into a string in which recognized numeric phrases are replaced by their integer representations, while preserving non-numeric words." text2int]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> textnum </REF>: string "The input text containing spelled-out numbers and ordinary words; hyphens are replaced with spaces before parsing."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> curstring </REF>: string "The transformed text with recognized number words converted to integer strings and ordinary words preserved."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Replace all '-' characters in textnum with spaces. RESULT textnum]
            [COMMAND Set current to 0. RESULT current]
            [COMMAND Set result to 0. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Set curstring to an empty string. RESULT curstring]
            [COMMAND Set onnumber to False. RESULT onnumber]
            [COMMAND For each word in textnum.split(), select the appropriate number-word branch for the current word. RESULT word]
            [COMMAND After the loop, if onnumber is True, append repr(result + current) to curstring. RESULT curstring]
            [COMMAND Return curstring. RESULT curstring]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: The current word is in self.ordinal_words.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over word from textnum.split(), in the ordinal-word branch, set scale to 1. RESULT scale]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over word from textnum.split(), in the ordinal-word branch, set increment to self.ordinal_words[word]. RESULT increment]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over word from textnum.split(), in the ordinal-word branch, update current = current * scale + increment. RESULT current]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over word from textnum.split(), in the ordinal-word branch, set onnumber to True. RESULT onnumber]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: The current word is not in self.ordinal_words.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over word from textnum.split(), in the non-ordinal-word branch, for each (ending, replacement) in self.ordinal_endings, if word ends with ending, replace the matching suffix by setting word = word[:-len(ending)] + replacement. RESULT word]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over word from textnum.split(), in the non-ordinal-word branch, if word is not in self.numwords and onnumber is True, append repr(result + current) + ' ' to curstring. RESULT curstring]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over word from textnum.split(), in the non-ordinal-word branch, if word is not in self.numwords, append word + ' ' to curstring. RESULT curstring]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over word from textnum.split(), in the non-ordinal-word branch, if word is not in self.numwords, set result to 0. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over word from textnum.split(), in the non-ordinal-word branch, if word is not in self.numwords, set current to 0. RESULT current]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over word from textnum.split(), in the non-ordinal-word branch, if word is not in self.numwords, set onnumber to False. RESULT onnumber]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over word from textnum.split(), in the non-ordinal-word branch, if word is in self.numwords, set scale to self.numwords[word][0]. RESULT scale]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over word from textnum.split(), in the non-ordinal-word branch, if word is in self.numwords, set increment to self.numwords[word][1]. RESULT increment]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over word from textnum.split(), in the non-ordinal-word branch, if word is in self.numwords, update current = current * scale + increment. RESULT current]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over word from textnum.split(), in the non-ordinal-word branch, if word is in self.numwords and scale > 100, add current to result. RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over word from textnum.split(), in the non-ordinal-word branch, if word is in self.numwords and scale > 100, set current to 0. RESULT current]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over word from textnum.split(), in the non-ordinal-word branch, if word is in self.numwords, set onnumber to True. RESULT onnumber]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
Words2Numbers.is_valid_input:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Replaces hyphens with spaces and validates that every resulting word is either a known ordinal word or can be transformed by ordinal suffix replacement into a recognized number word in self.numwords; returns True only when all words pass." is_valid_input]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "Converter instance containing ordinal_words, ordinal_endings, and numwords attributes."
        <REF> textnum </REF>: string "Text phrase to validate as a number string."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: boolean "True if every word after hyphen normalization and ordinal suffix replacement is found in self.numwords; otherwise False."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Replace every hyphen '-' in textnum with a space ' ' and assign the resulting string back to textnum. RESULT textnum]
            [COMMAND Split textnum on whitespace and iterate over each resulting word token. RESULT word]
            [COMMAND Within the outer loop over word, when word is not in self.ordinal_words, iterate in order over each (ending, replacement) pair in self.ordinal_endings. RESULT ending_replacement_pair]
            [COMMAND Within that inner loop, if the current word ends with ending, set word to the prefix before that ending plus replacement. RESULT word]
            [COMMAND Within the outer loop, after the inner loop finishes, check whether the transformed word is in self.numwords; if it is, continue to the next word. RESULT is_known_number_word]
            [COMMAND After all words have been processed and validated, return True. RESULT True]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: The current word is in self.ordinal_words.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Within the outer loop over word, skip the current word and continue with the next token from textnum.split(). RESULT next_word]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: After ordinal suffix processing, the current word is not in self.numwords.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return False immediately, without processing any remaining words. RESULT False]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
